title: SPECTRA: State-Space Exogenous Context and Temporal-Frequency Resolution Architecture for Probabilistic Energy Forecasting
note: Abstract (v1 only, stat.ML/cs.LG, submitted to IEEE Trans. Power Systems): trained architecture splitting deterministic and residual streams with exogenous context aligned to both, quantile outputs. Best CRPS in 14 of 18 load/price/solar/wind settings; average CRPS 5.74% and upper-tail quantile risk 7.27% below the strongest baselines. No code link on the abstract page.

title: SPECTRA (HTML full text): data and protocol
note: Data: ECL (321 clients, hourly, 2012-2014), Open Power System Data (hourly, 2015-2017), GEFCom2014 (2011-2014, temperature/calendar/holiday covariates), plus a 15-min wind/PV case study. Chronological 7:1:2 split, no test dates or day counts. Input 168 h; horizons 12/24/36 (short) and 72/120/168 (long), averaged. Three seeds; no intervals or significance tests. No pre-registration mentioned.

title: SPECTRA (HTML full text): baselines, inputs, compute
note: Baselines: DeepAR, TFT, TADNet, TiDE, TimeXer, Autoformer, PatchTST, DLinear, all trained with a quantile head; no regression or foundation-model baseline. Covariates for ECL and OPS are not named; whether weather is actual or forecast, and whether baselines got the same exogenous inputs, is not stated. Trained on one NVIDIA A30 GPU; parameter count not given. Code at github.com/yedadasd/SPECTRA.

title: yedadasd/SPECTRA: official implementation
note: Repository exists: training code (run.py, scripts per dataset), 14 commits, 1 star, no releases, no licence shown, no pretrained checkpoints, no datasets (user prepares CSVs). Needs Python 3.10, PyTorch with CUDA and mamba-ssm; GPU recommended. README repeats 14 of 18, top-two in 17, 5.74% CRPS, 7.27% rho90, 1.78% rho50; the results table is an image, not read. Last commit date not seen.
